plan: My private value is $9. In a second-price sealed auction with three bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since the values are independently drawn and this is a single round, I'll bid exactly my private value of $9.

My private value is $40. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item when it's worth more to you
2. Bidding more doesn't increase your expected profit
3. I'm neutral about risk, so I want to maximize my expected value
4. I'll bid exactly $40, which ensures I win if my value is highest and pays the third-highest bid
